title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: The Government of Nepal, represented by the Ministry of Labour, Employment, and Social Security (MOLESS) has developed guidelines on apprenticeship programme and work-based learning. In 2022, the Employers organization (EO) adopted it with some improvement by aligning it with the ILO standard on quality apprenticeship. Following this adoption, the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FNCCI) developed the curriculum and manuals for work-based learning of four occupations (Cardamum Processor, Fishery Technician, Ginger Processor and Tour Product Developer). The ILO, with RBSA funding, organized briefing programmes for tripartite constituents on ILO approaches for work-based learning, formal and informal apprenticeship. Support was extended to adapt the Government’s apprenticeship and work-based learning guidelines and align them with Labour Standards relevant to apprenticeship. Through an Implementation Agreement, the sector-based industries were provided with opportunities to test the adapted guideline and to make further recommendations for improvement.

description.narrative: The Member Business Organisations (MBOs), especially Federation of National Cottage and Small Industries (FNCSI), Federation of Women Entrepreneurs (FWEAN) and enterprises associated with Sector -based industries implemented skills and employment programmes targeting the returnee migrants, with emphasis on women and workers in informal sectors most affected by COVID-19. Priority was given for those job seekers who were registered as unemployed/under-employed with Public Employment Service Centres. This also helped them access necessary employment services extended through these sectors. The programme has been appreciated not just because it provided training to vulnerable workers, but also it provided opportunities to enterprises to train and retrain workers that were laid -off during covid. In order to increase their post-training employment opportunities, work-based learning method was applied for training. Around 500 informal workers, including returnee female migrants, have been provided with work-based learning opportunities and most of them employed in selected sectors (agriculture, tourism, construction, and manufacturing). ILO through the available RBSA and RBTC funds, capacitated the MBOS available and interested on providing work-based learning opportunities to vulnerable workers. Shared best practices with the constituents and provided necessary technical advice for establishing and operationalizing a tripartite committee for skills development. EO was also supported to organize job fair at local level in order to provide information to job seekers on potential job opportunities, available vacancies and the skills needed for these jobs. To meet the specific needs of returnee migrants for their integration in labour market, skills profiling was conducted among 600 returnees during the covid pandemic.
